newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Yield spread Portugal bonds/bunds hits record low.
newsitem.headline: Yield spread Portugal bonds/bunds hits record low.

text.p: The yield spread between 10-year Portuguese Treasury bonds and equivalent Bunds stood at a record low of 195 basis points on Friday, dealers said.
"The 10-year spread between Portuguese bonds and German Bunds is below 200 basis points (bp), its lowest ever level," said one trader.
The yield on February 1996 bonds stood at 8.09 percent compared with April 1996 Bunds at 6.14 percent.
The differential has fallen from around 228 basis points this month.

"The narrowing of spreads with Germany is a result of buying by foreign investors who are also active in Spain. They believe that Portuguese fundamentals allow for a further narrowing of this yield differential," said one trader.
"The question is simple. If Spain can join the single currency among the first group of countries, Portugal is even better placed to do so," said one director of fixed-rate debt.

"The budget deficit looks very positive and could be at 3.0 percent of gross domestic product (GDP) in 1997. Inflation could be 2.5 percent next year and the escudo has been consistently strong," he said.
